public_reads.purpose: Democracy Now! article on the Rogers/Aegis story
public_reads.finding: Body says Drop Site News reports Mike Rogers’s personal wealth rose after he became House Intelligence Committee chair in 2011, attributing much of the change to marriage to Kristi Clemens Rogers, a senior Aegis executive; says Aegis won billions in contracts during his tenure; says the campaign sent Drop Site a cease-and-desist demanding correction/retraction and Drop Site stands by its report. These are claims summarized by Democracy Now!, not independently verified by this check. No report methodology, financial-disclosure calculations, contract docket or campaign letter was reviewed.

public_reads.finding: Homepage response did not expose a Rogers/Aegis story link or matching article text in the locally parsed body; the original Drop Site report itself was not retrieved.

baseline_and_comparison.michigan: Existing decision 211 (2026-10-18) records the Michigan Democratic-win primary YES 55% / NO 45%, broad YES 30–80 range, based then on YouGov/Rasmussen and official six-candidate listing; stated mixed fundraising did not quantify votes. The new Democracy Now! item adds a potentially adverse allegation about Rogers; this bounded check did not verify it against primary records or measure voter response. No new Michigan vote-intention poll was found in captured sources.
baseline_and_comparison.house_races: The approval headline is national presidential job approval. It is not a NY-01, CA-06, or ME-02 ballot/matchup result; no district-specific evidence was verified from the captured sources.

poll_status.alert_claim: Alert metadata/agent reason says record-low 31%; direct France24 and Reuters bodies inaccessible. Treat as unverified alert framing here.
secondary_leads_only: Search-index/aggregator leads diverged by population: 31% approve among 1,679 adults (field dates reported Oct 16–19) versus 34% among 1,279 registered voters. They must not be combined or treated as a verified common estimand.
Parent supplied the existing official Ipsos Sep 21 release as baseline: 32% approve among 1,277 adults, fielded Sep 17–20. The release was not fetched in this check.
Parent separately identified the official Ipsos mid-October primary link; parent will capture its exact body/PDF. This agent did not read it.
poll_status.interpretation_limit: National approval is distinct from vote preference and from state/district candidate matchups. No updated approval number, fielding dates, population or sample is adopted pending the parent’s primary Ipsos capture.

coverage_gap: Original Drop Site News story body not retrieved; current Ipsos mid-October poll release not captured by this agent; France24 body 403; guessed Reuters path 401; exact Google News destination remained a consent page. Primary details remain unresolved within the six-request cap.
